purpose: Provide deterministic escalation targets, deadlines, and actions by blocker severity and blocker type.

severity_levels.description: Stops the current round or puts integration safety at immediate risk.
Blocks a package from hitting the planned round objective or risks missing a dependency deadline.
Reduces throughput or leaves a work item waiting, but the round can continue elsewhere.
Needs tracking and response, but does not threaten round stability today.

matrix.required_action: Open escalation event, page the dependency owner, and create an emergency handoff if ownership must move.
Reprioritize the dependency queue and publish the revised due time.
Monitor the open request and keep the item visible in coordination snapshots.
Track in backlog and close when the dependency response lands.
Freeze downstream execution, publish the scoping decision owner, and reissue the affected handoff or packet.
Schedule immediate clarification and update acceptance criteria.
Queue for clarification before the next planned checkpoint.
Record the ambiguity and resolve during the next operator review cycle.
Stop impacted work, preserve evidence, and reroute unaffected work to keep the round moving.
Isolate the failing subsystem and publish the workaround if one exists.
Track the degraded path and update the next checkpoint with impact scope.
Record and close once a stable workaround is documented.
Block integration, preserve evidence, and demand corrective action before the merge window opens.
Require remediation plan and new evidence before the item can return to in progress.
Track as a conditional acceptance risk and review at the next checkpoint.
Record and clear when evidence is refreshed or the waiver path is documented.

global_rules: Every sev1 and sev2 blocker must appear in the next coordination snapshot.
Escalation events are immutable after publication except for appended history entries.
Closing an escalation requires a resolution summary and evidence refs.
